newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-IAMA sees nine pct year profit growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-IAMA sees nine pct year profit growth.

text.p: Rural merchandising group IAMA Ltd said on Tuesday that its third quarter sales results were above budget and it was hoping to repeat the nine percent profit growth seen in the first half through the year to September 30.
"I would hope so, excluding any unforeseen events," IAMA managing director Danny Bourke told reporters when asked if IAMA could repeat its first half profit growth.
IAMA's net profit rose nine percent to A$6.81 million in the six months to March 31, after having risen 80 percent to A$15.54 million in the full 1995/96 year on sales of A$787.7 million.
Earlier, Bourke told a Securities Institute function the group was on target to achieve sales of over A$900 million for the full year.

Bourke also said the company was undergoing a strategic review and had decided to focus on its core activities and concentrate less on growth through acquisitions in the wake of its unsuccessful takeover bid for Primac Holdings Ltd.
"We've just completed a strategic planning session-workshop," Bourke said, adding a formal strategic review would be completed in the next three months.
"We've decided that we'll spend more time concentrating on our core businesses, rather than be out there looking for acquisitions," he said.
He acknowledged that there had been some concern in the market that the recent growth had been too widespread and focus had been lost.
IAMA may even look at selling some assets, he said.
"We'll look to rationalise, even in some of our own branches, depending on how they're performing.
Growth would tend in future to come from efficiency gains and organic growth from existing businesses rather than through acquisition.
IAMA's shares were down one cent at A$2.85 at 3.05 p.m. (0505 GMT).
